title: All things work together (Romans 8:28–30)
hookLine: for good, to those who love God
carry: a good thread in the weave

lines: WHAT DOES THE VERSE ACTUALLY SAY?
cards: It shows up on mugs and sympathy cards, and at funerals, said by someone trying to help: everything happens for a reason. Sometimes it lands gently, sometimes like a slap.
Tell someone whose child is sick that it's all for a reason, and watch their face. Some people assume the line comes from the Bible.
The verse it gets pinned to is in Romans chapter eight, and that verse says something different. So what does it actually say?

teach.b: Here it is, in the King James Bible: "And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose." First, what it doesn't say: that all things are good.
Paul has just spent a paragraph on suffering, groaning, a world in labor pains. He's not pretending cancer is good, or cruelty, or loss. Second, what it does say.
Work together is one word in Greek, synergei; you can hear our word synergy in it. Things that are not good in themselves are worked together, woven, into something good.
A weaver uses dark threads as well as bright ones, and the pattern only shows from the other side. That picture isn't Paul's, but it helps with his word. And who does the working?
The verse is about those who love God and are called according to his purpose, so some readers hear God as the subject: God works all things together for good. God is the weaver, not luck.

teach.h: A GOLDEN CHAIN, READ THREE WAYS.
teach.b: Then verses twenty-nine and thirty trace a golden chain: those God foreknew, he predestined, called, justified and glorified. Christians read that chain differently.
Reformed Christians, following Calvin, stress God's sovereign choice. Methodists and others, following Wesley, stress that God's foreknowledge leaves room for human freedom.

teach.h: ALL THINGS WORK TOGETHER FOR GOOD.
teach.b: Catholic and Orthodox teaching holds God's grace and human cooperation together. Each finds the same comfort in it: the story is held.
And this week, peace with God, Adam and Christ, dead to sin, the wretched man, no condemnation, the groaning world, all gets woven together.

how: Some Christians hold onto Romans 8:28 in hard seasons, and pastors often explain it carefully so it isn't used to call suffering good.

o: everything that happens is good in itself
every event has a reason planned in advance
woven together into good, though not good itself

games.q: what's inside the verse — tap the pairs.

s: just before this verse, Paul has been writing about suffering and groaning
the verse comes right after a world in labor pains; it does not call suffering good.
Paul says the hard things themselves are good
he says they work together for good; the weaver is only a picture to help hear his word.
all Christians read verses 29 and 30 the same way
Reformed, Wesleyan, Catholic and Orthodox Christians read the golden chain differently.

games.q: a friend's child is in the hospital. you want to comfort them with Romans 8:28. what does the verse actually give you?
o: this is good, it happened for a reason.
even this can be woven into good.
nothing bad happens to those who love God.
games.why: the verse says all things work together for good, not that all things are good. Paul has just spoken of a world groaning in pain.

practice: Bring to mind something hard, and don't call it good, it may not be; just turn it over gently, the way you'd turn a woven cloth to see the back, and look for one thread of good worked into it: a kindness, something you learned, a friend who showed up.
If you can't find one yet, that's all right; Paul says we know, not that we always see. If you pray, hand the hard thing to God, the weaver.

wordCard.voice: Synergei. Paul's Greek word for worked together: not that hard things are good, but that even they get woven into good.

orig.note: Greek: works together, cooperates. the root of our word synergy.

carryVoice: Your line: a good thread in the weave. Dark threads belong too. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
